actionable_steps.citation: Discover the God within you — SSS Vol 24 (1991), 1991-07-26
actionable_steps.step: Practise self-enquiry: when you say 'my body' or 'my mind', notice that the speaker — the 'I' — is the seer, separate from them.
Step into your day with the conviction 'I am the Atma, the Divine spark in me' — then neither success can spoil you nor defeat dishearten you.

actionable_steps.citation: Discharge your duties with a sense of surrender to God — SSS Vol 39 (2006), 2006-01-14
actionable_steps.step: In whatever practice you do — japa, prayer, work — focus the mind on the Atma itself, with purity of heart.
Watch for the sleep of 'I' and 'Mine' in small daily choices, and gently drop it; the Atma shines when mine-ness ends.

definition.citation: Vision Of The Atma — SSS Vol 34 (2001), 2001-02-21
definition.quote: First of all, understand what Atma means. The principle of 'I' that is present in everybody is Atma... Truth is one, not two.

discourses.quote: Confirm in your faith that you are the Atma, which is the Divine Spark in you, and then, move into the world as heroes whom success cannot spoil or defeat cannot dishearten.

A mere five-minute inquiry will convince you that you are not the body, the senses, the mind, the intelligence, the name, or the form, but that you are the Atma Itself, the same Atma that appears as all this variety.

discourses.citation: Discover the God within you — SSS Vol 24 (1991), 1991-07-26
discourses.quote: The wisdom that 'I am the Atma' should blossom in every human being. It is only when this wisdom dawns that man can have direct experience of the Divine.
Atma means that which is filled with bliss. You cannot secure this bliss from the things of the world. All the pleasures you experience are fleeting.

make_it_real: You are not the body you carry or the thoughts you think — you are the Atma. Live this one day from that depth.
title: Atma / True Self

vahinis.quote: The Atma is present everywhere and is in everything. It is unaffected. It is omnipresent, like ether (akasa)... Atma is everything; there is nothing that is not Atma. Atma is full and free. Knowing this is the highest truth, the fullest knowledge (jnana).
The Atma, which observes all these activities, that is 'You'... You are the Atma. Until this truth is realised, you sleep the sleep of 'I' and 'Mine'.
